answer.explanation: Redis is configured with maxmemory=8MB and policy=noeviction, but its baseline dataset already uses ~12MB (used_memory 12246752 > maxmemory 8388608, current_eviction_exceeded_time still counting up). With noeviction, any write command that would grow memory further is rejected with an OOM error instead of evicting keys, and total_error_replies is already 16 despite very light traffic. As a result, most of the api's RPUSH calls to enqueue a job on the 'jobs' list fail; the api catches this failure and falls back to processing the job synchronously in-request (matching the worker's own ~2.0s per-job processing time seen in 'processed job ec4a073d2868 in 2.0s'), which is why POST /jobs latency jumped to a very consistent ~2.0-2.03s while returning 200 instead of the fast 202 seen for the one job that *did* make it onto the queue. Because the api swallows the Redis error and completes the work itself, the error rate stays normal even though the queueing path is broken — the symptom only shows up as latency. The queue length staying at 0 and the worker having processed only a single job total (despite dozens of successful POST /jobs) confirms the async path is essentially bypassed.

answer.explanation: GET /orders returns 5xx because the api's /health check reports db:"unreachable" and the api's own traceback shows every new postgres connection attempt failing with "remaining connection slots are reserved". Inspecting postgres directly shows why: max_connections is capped at 100, and right now all 100 slots are consumed, with 93 of them owned by a role called "batch" (application_name "psql", rolconnlimit -1, i.e. unlimited) that is not one of the api/worker/nginx/redis/loadgen stack components. This "batch" actor has opened dozens of psql sessions and is holding them (largely idle, no state shown) instead of releasing them, so when the api or worker try to open a new connection there are 0 non-reserved slots left, producing the FATAL "remaining connection slots are reserved for roles with privileges of the 'pg_use_reserved_connections' role" error seen both in postgres' log and the api traceback. The worker itself is still healthy and actively processing jobs (connects as role 'svc'), and nginx/redis show no issue, confirming the fault is not in the application code path but in an external/batch workload against postgres exhausting the shared connection pool that the api depends on for GET /orders.
